message.reasoning:
I need to respond to a Monopoly trade offer.

I'm in jail with $875 cash and a get-out-of-jail card. I own four streets: Mediterranean, St James, New York, and Pennsylvania Avenue. The opponent offered North Carolina Avenue for $180. I previously countered at $35. Paying $180 would give them $244, which they could use to build houses on their pink monopoly. North Carolina does not complete a set because Pacific is still unowned.

I'm in jail, so I can't land on Pacific. $180 would leave me with $695 cash, which is still vulnerable to dark blue hits from p2. My prior plan was to cap the offer at $35 so p1 stays under $100 and cannot buy a pink house. If they refuse, I will not raise again. North Carolina's mortgage value is $150.

The $180 offer is $30 above North Carolina's mortgage value. Accepting it would give the opponent enough cash to build two pink houses, making that color set dangerous once I leave jail. Dark blue three-house rents are $1,400 and $1,100, so I cannot afford either even after paying $180. Rejecting the offer is now being considered.

Rejecting the offer is risky. The opponent could mortgage North Carolina for $150, giving them $214 to build pink houses. Accepting would give them $244 instead. North Carolina has little strategic value right now because Pacific is still unowned and I am in jail.

Any counter offer above $35 would give the opponent exactly $100, enough to buy one pink house. The only viable options are accept, reject, or counter.

Rejecting the offer is the better choice. Paying $180 would give the opponent $244, while mortgaging North Carolina for $150 would only give them $214. Mortgaging also removes the property's trade value. I will reject the offer.

A property swap would not help. I cannot give up my orange streets without losing my path to a monopoly. Pennsylvania would complete the opponent's green set, and Mediterranean is useless to them. They need cash to build, so a zero-cash counter offer is impossible.

I will reject the trade. The public message will state that $180 still funds the opponent's pink houses and North Carolina does not complete a set while Pacific remains unowned, so I will not pay above $35.
